Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office files ordinary paperwork through versioned document registers, metadata fields, and audited channels, maintaining a single source of truth for each record item, with changes logged by account, date, and document reference.

2) What occurred: The actor accessed the component master register for the affected airframe and entered a replacement part entry using the identifier of an approved component while substituting the unapproved supplier's material. In the maintenance log, the actor amended the part serial number field to match the approved part number, adjusted the installation date to precede the procurement date of the unapproved item, and updated the inspection sign-off field to show a completed airworthiness check. The part history document was altered to remove the original entry for the unapproved component and insert a fabricated traceability record with a forged batch number and a backdated certificate of conformance reference. A service release certificate was generated through the records channel with a modified airworthiness status field set to "compliant," and the document was routed to the regulator's submission portal under the airline's account.

3) Materials/access observed: The actor used a named maintenance engineer account with elevated edit permissions on the records management system. Artifacts included the component master register file, the maintenance log entry with overwritten fields, the part history document with a deleted original record and an inserted fabricated entry, a service release certificate with a modified status field, and an outbound transmission to the regulator's portal from the airline's account.

4) Indicators & artifacts: Audit trail gaps where the component master register shows a single edit event without a corresponding procurement record. The maintenance log contains a part serial number mismatch between the installed item and the traceability document. The part history document exhibits a deleted record marker and an inserted entry with an out-of-sequence batch number. The service release certificate carries a status field value inconsistent with the underlying inspection data. The regulator submission channel shows a document upload from the airline account with a timestamp preceding the completion date of the associated inspection record.
